segments.translation_text: Those who cause harm create positive conditions for accomplishing patience, therefore they are actually beneficial. Thinking in this way and not retaliating is a benefit in this life. Through this, they become devoted and engage in the path of virtue, which will be of benefit in the next life. Thus, sentient beings are completely matured. The Ornament states:

segments.translation_text: The opposite of patience that should be discarded is anger. The antidote is realization of the selflessness of phenomena, through which one possesses primordial wisdom of non-conceptualization of the three cycles. The outcome that is a temporary result is that the wishes of those who cause harm are completely fulfilled because one does not respond to their harm. The ultimate result is placing the harmers in the nirvana of one of the three vehicles according to their motivation. Thus beings are completely matured through the four dharmas.

segments.translation_text: Concerning the patience of realizing the certainty of phenomena, because of realizing that all phenomena are perceivable yet lack inherent nature like a magical show, when material success occurs then attachment, conceit, and the like will not be experienced, so there is no fear of the defilements. Thus there is no fear of the profundity of Dharma. It is said:

segments.translation_text: The good quality of vastness is disregarding suffering such as giving even the head and other limbs, which is extremely difficult for ordinary beings to perform, and especially not retaliating no matter what harm human beings cause. The good quality of freedom from materialism is having no desire for higher rebirth, no inability to respond, no other fears, and no hope of reward. The good quality of great purpose is placing those gathered by patience in one of the three types of enlightenment according to their motivation. The good quality of inexhaustibility is continuing without ceasing, even in the state of nirvana without remainder.

segments.translation_text: The Sons of Jinas are able to tolerate things extremely difficult to endure, as well as human harm. They neither seek higher birth, nor are unable, nor fearful, nor seeking reward; With unsurpassable patience, they place all beings in the three types of enlightenment. As that patience is completely sealed by primordial wisdom, it is inexhaustible in this world.

They neither seek higher birth, nor are unable, nor fearful, nor seeking reward;
With unsurpassable patience, they place all beings in the three types of enlightenment.
As that patience is completely sealed by primordial wisdom, it is inexhaustible in this world.

The Sutra of Manjushri’s Enjoyment states:

segments.translation_html:
Carrying the pain of hatred in the mind,
The awareness will not experience mental peace,
Nor will joy and happiness be attained;
Sleep is elusive and one becomes unstable.

segments.translation_text: Anger is a sickness that wearies the body and mind. There is no happiness or peace when the mind is angry, and one cannot find mental happiness or physical comfort. As a result, there is no sleep at night, and the mind is constantly unstable and greatly disturbed due to the blazing fire of hatred.

segments.translation_html:
In the occurrence of what is unwanted, and
Interference with what is wanted,
Mental unhappiness finds its food
Which increases hatred, and one is destroyed.

This enemy that is hatred is good for nothing but harming me by destroying my virtue and the like.

segments.translation_text: If under careful analysis whatever suffering occurs, such as harm, etc., can be repaired, then why feel unhappy? It is unnecessary. Rather exert oneself in the act of repair, and discard unhappiness. On the other hand, if nothing can be repaired, what is the benefit of unhappiness? There is no benefit, only greater harm. Therefore, whatever suffering occurs, discard unhappiness and accept the suffering as a positive support on the path.

segments.translation_text: When oneself, relatives, or friends experience suffering, which means physical or mental pain; scorn, which means being disregarded; harsh words, which means being struck in the heart; or malicious gossip, which means criticism, these are undesirable. Due to these undesirable things, the mind feels unhappy, which gives rise to anger. Another source of anger is interference with what one desires, such as happiness, respect, praise, and fame.

segments.translation_html:
Causes of happiness occur occasionally.
Causes of suffering extremely often,
Without suffering, there is no renunciation,
Therefore, O Mind, stand firm.

segments.translation_text: In samsara, the virtues that are the cause of happiness only rarely occur, therefore it is rare to find happiness. The causes from which suffering arise are the great myriad of nonvirtues, so myriad sufferings effortlessly arise. Therefore, discard an unhappy mind and patiently accept whatever occurs, thinking that it is a result that has arisen from a previous cause.

segments.translation_text: Those who worship the goddess Uma, who turned the great god Shiva away from his austerity, offer their bodies in a fire puja. At Karnatapa in southern India, during solar and lunar eclipses, some Hindus who wish to attain the level of Brahma cut off their heads. Others practice burning themselves in five huge fires, piercing themselves by jumping on an upward-pointing trident, cutting themselves and the like. Such violent practices cause great suffering, yet do not produce the desired result. If they can tolerate such things, then when I perform hardship in the practice of the Mahayana path for the purpose of attaining the ultimate result of Buddhahood and liberation for oneself and others, it is unsuitable be afraid. I should voluntarily be patient and happy.

segments.translation_text: If we must go through various meaningless unpleasant sensations such the bites of bees and snakes, weariness due to hunger and thirst, and irritating itches, then, do not be weak and impatient for the purpose of accomplishing the great goal of enlightenment. Do not allow patience to weaken when experiencing the minor sufferings of weariness and tiredness due to heat, cold, rain, and wind, or the suffering of being ill, bound, struck, or cut, because if one does so, patience will weaken and the harm and suffering will grow stronger and increase.

segments.translation_text: The minds of the wise, who are skilled in meditation on patience, remain filled with clear awareness and joy. They are not disturbed even by severe suffering and unpleasantness. They exert themselves in battle between the defilements to be abandoned such as hatred, and the antidotes to be adopted such as patience. Even if some additional harm is incurred on this battlefield, disregard it for the purpose of accomplishing the great goal.

segments.translation_text: As explained above, renunciation does not arise without suffering. Other good qualities that arise from suffering are: suffering makes one wish to be freed from suffering; disappointment dispels pride, conceit, and arrogance; personally experiencing a small portion of suffering develops compassion for those whose suffering is greater; by thinking that this is the result of sinful actions, one resists non-virtue and delights in performing virtue; and one develops joyful faith in the Buddha who taught the method of pacifying suffering. Meditate on these and voluntarily accept suffering.

Great sources of suffering such as jaundice,

segments.translation_text: One may think that although suffering itself should be tolerated, it is appropriate to be angry at those who cause the harm that produced the suffering. If that were the case, one should be angry at the various blood, bile, wind, and other illnesses that produce so many terrible sufferings. Concerning this point, some may argue that one does not become angry in this case because there was no intention to produce suffering; it arose through the gathering of conditions. If that were the case why become angry with beings who possess a mind? It is inappropriate to be angry with beings, because these causers of harm lack independence; they are influenced by previous karmic conditions.

segments.translation_html:
Beings become angry for simple reasons. Although they do not wish anger to arise. Although it does not wish to develop, Anger arises just like that.[p.199][[A Commentary on Shantideva's Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas]]
Gyaltsen, Lama Kalsang, and Ani Kunga Chodron, trans. ''A Commentary on Shantideva's Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas Written by Sazang Mati Panchen: Known as An Extremely Clear Illumination of the Meaning of the Text''. Walden, NY: Tsechen Kunchab Ling, 2019. First edition published by The Yeshe Dorje Foundation in 2006.

segments.translation_text: Those who cause harm do not think, "Now I will give rise to anger.” If various conditions occur, it arises naturally. Even if they do think, "Now I will give rise to anger,” if the necessary conditions are not fully assembled, anger will not arise. Therefore, in both examples, anger arises from similar conditions. Whether or not the cause of harm possesses intentionality, it is inappropriate to become angry.

segments.translation_text: Also, because they believe it to be permanent, there could never be any cessation of the experience of the object. But this is not valid because it would logically follow that the subject, which is the mind, would have to cease when the object ceases. It can be seen that mind’s experience of objects is periodic, not permanent. This demonstrates that the primal substance and the self are neither creators nor independently arisen.

segments.translation_text: If the self meets other simultaneously arising conditions but remains the same as before, then what did those conditions contribute to the self that did not exist before? They could not have contributed anything. Hence, how can the so-called simultaneously arising conditions connect with the self? There could not be any connection because they are separate entities, and therefore cannot be connected into a unitary self. Also, they are not related in the sense that one arises from the other, because they are not a cause and a result.

segments.translation_text: If beings were able to act independently according to their wishes without being under the power of other conditions, then because no sentient being wishes to experience suffering and all wish to experience happiness, no being would ever experience unhappiness. This is obviously not the case. Therefore, it is demonstrated that anger, which is a type of unhappiness, arises under the power of other conditions. Thus, because the causers of harm lack independence, develop compassion toward those who suffer thus and do not feel anger.

segments.translation_text: The careless behavior of ordinary deluded sentient beings brings them under the power of others. Due to a lack of heedfulness, they harm themselves with thorns, stones, gravel, and other materials. Wishing to gain material wealth and women, they even crave others’ wealth and others’ wives. segments.translation_html:
The careless behavior of ordinary deluded sentient beings brings them under the power of others. Due to a lack of heedfulness, they harm themselves with thorns, stones, gravel, and other materials. Wishing to gain material wealth[p.203][[An Extremely Clear Illumination of the Meaning of the Text]]
and women, they even crave others’ wealth and others’ wives. If they are unable to fulfill their desires, they may torture themselves by going without food and drink and thus fasting, starving, or torturing themselves.

For example, when burned by a fire, it is not right to feel anger toward the fire because it is the nature of fire to burn. The two cases are similar.

segments.translation_text: On the other hand, if it is not the nature of sentient beings to harm others, then the harm is a temporary stain that can be abandoned, which means that it does not permanently exist. The nature of the mind of sentient beings is clear light, which is peaceful, unchangeable, and naturally perfectly pure. Thus, it is not right to feel anger toward sentient beings because their nature is flawless. For instance, although space is naturally pure, smoke and mist temporarily arise within it. It is not right to feel angry toward the sky because of the obscuration caused by the smoke and mist. This is similar.

segments.translation_text: If injured by a physical weapon such as a sword or stick, one can put it aside, confident that the weapon cannot independently injure. One should not be angry at the striker or thrower who wields the weapon, thinking that he is the causer of harm, because he also is not independent. His action was caused by the defilement of hatred. If anger is felt, it is appropriate to be angry at the defilement of hatred itself, not at the person. Instead, develop compassion.

segments.translation_text: In many previous lives, I harmed other sentient beings in various ways, such as striking them with sticks, beating them with weapons, and stealing their possessions. Due to the cause of having harmed other sentient beings by violent actions, as a result, I am experiencing these various sufferings caused by others, because of the infallible link between cause and result.

Both their weapons and my body
Are the cause of suffering.
If their weapons and my body are both extended,
To whom should I feel angry first?

segments.wylie: rgyu tshogs pa las 'bras bu 'byung ba ni kun rdzob kyi chos nyid yin pas gnod byed de yi mtshon cha dang gnod bya bdag gi lus gnyis ka'ang sdug bsngal gyi rgyu yin par mtshungs te/_dgra des mtshon phyung zhing bdag gis lus phyung nas rmas pa la sogs pa sdug bsngal myong ba na/_rang gzhan gnyis po gang zhig la ni khro bar bya ste/_nyes pa mnyam pas gzhan kho na la lhag par khro ba ni mi rigs so/_/
segments.translation_text: The production of a result from the assembly of causes is a natural conventional law. Therefore, both the weapon which causes the harm and my own body which is the object that is harmed are equally the causes of suffering. The enemy gave rise to the weapon, and I gave rise to my body; as a result injury occurred and suffering was experienced. Where should I direct my anger, toward myself or the enemy? As both are equally at fault, it is not suitable to be angry with only one.

segments.translation_html:
This abscess of a human form
Suffers so that touch is intolerable;
If I hold it as a self with blind craving.
At whom should I be angry when it is harmed?

segments.wylie: gzhan yang 'jig pa sla zhing 'tsho ba dka' la khrag dang chu ser la sogs pa smin pa'i shu ba rnam pa mi yi gzugs brnyan 'dra ba gzhan gyis reg pa tsam du yang mi bzod pa'i sdug bsngal can 'di khams gsum la sred pas shes rab kyi mig mdongs shing long ba bdag [p.-188] [[rab gsal snang ba]] gis gzung bar gyur na/_lus de la gnod pa gzhan su la khro ste khro bar mi rigs shing rang la khro bar rigs te lus bzung bas nyes pa ba'i phyir ro/_/
segments.translation_text: This human body so easily disintegrates and it is difficult to sustain its life. This ripened abscess in the form of a human body is merely a heap of blood, pus, and the like. When it is barely touched by other objects, it suffers. If I cling to such a body as this, which lacks the eye of wisdom and clings to physical existence in the three worlds which is the nature of suffering, how could it be right to be angry toward others when harm occurs? In fact I should be angry at myself for clinging to a body.

segments.translation_html:
Although the childish do not desire suffering.
Due to craving for the causes of suffering,
One is harmed by one’s own misdeeds.
Why be angry with others?

segments.wylie: gang 'bras bu mi 'dod na de'i rgyu spang bar rigs pa yin pa la byis pa so so'i skye bo rmongs pa rnams ni 'bras bu sdug bsngal myong bar mi 'dod kyang sdug bsngal gyi rgyu sdig pa sna tshogs spyod pa la brkam zhing chags pas na/_rang gi mi dge ba'i nyes pas rang la sdug bsngal gyis gnod par gyur pa'i phyir gzhan la khro zhing bkon du ci zhig yod de khro bar mi rigs so/_/
segments.translation_text: In reality, if a result is not desired, its cause should be discarded. However, ordinary childlike beings are deluded for they do not wish to experience the result of suffering, yet are strongly attached to and even crave the sin that is the cause of suffering. Sufferings are the result of one’s own sins, so is it suitable to be angry with others? It is not.

segments.translation_text: For example, the fearsome guardians of hell, the forest of razor-sharp leaves and other sufferings in the hell realms are produced by those beings' own previous sins. In the same way, these current sufferings and harms have been produced by my own sins. Therefore, why should I be angry toward others thinking that they have caused this harm? I should be angry only at myself.

segments.translation_html:
By the force of my own karma,
I encounter those who cause me harm.
If this forces those sentient beings into hell,
Won't I destroy them?

segments.translation_text: Due to the force of my previous negative karma, the enemies who cause me harm have appeared in this life. Their actions which cause me harm will cause them to fall into the lower realms, such as hell. Isn’t it I who am destroying them? Yes, it is. Therefore if there is anger, it is right for the enemies to be angry at me.

segments.translation_text: One may wonder whether because the causer of harm has created conditions for my accumulation of patience, won’t great merit arise for the causer of harm? segments.translation_text: Even if I am wealthy and live a long time, I will certainly experience the suffering of death. The pleasures of material wealth will not follow me at that time. For example, if in a dream, one experiences a hundred years of happiness and material wealth and then awakens, and then in another dream experiences a single moment of happiness and wealth, in both cases, the happiness of the dream does not follow into the awakened state. Likewise, neither the pleasures of a long, wealthy life, nor the pleasures of a short wealthy life will follow one after death, so they are similar.

segments.translation_text: Even if for a long time, the pleasures of wealth are experienced with many possessions gained in this life, in the end, at the time of death one must go as if all that wealth were stolen by thieves. When departing for the next world, one goes forth naked without clothing, empty-handed without wealth. Therefore, realize that material wealth is without essence.

segments.translation_text: One may think, "If I have a long, wealthy life, I will be able to make offerings and gifts, which will exhaust my sins and increase merit.” It is possible for wealth to be obtained according to Dharma. But if anger arises toward those who interfere with gaining that wealth, won’t that increase the sin which arises from anger and exhaust the merit that was accumulated through many eons of good deeds? Yes, it will.

segments.translation_text: Embodied beings incur harm both from beings that possess a mind and phenomena that lack a mind such as storms, wind, etc. Why feel anger only toward harm that arises from beings that possess a mind? We do not feel angry toward harm that occurs from phenomena that lack a mind. Therefore, it is inappropriate to be angry toward those that possess a mind. Be patient with them in the same way that one is patient with harm that arises from the elements.

segments.translation_text: Beings who cause harm produce this sin due to their lack of understanding of the inherent nature of phenomena. Those who are harmed become angry due to their lack of understanding of the inherent nature of phenomena. Which of the two is faultless? Both equally possess the fault of ignorance. Therefore, it is inappropriate to show partiality by being angry only at the causer of harm.

segments.translation_html:
Those actions that caused harm to others,
Why were they previously done?
Since everything depends upon karma,
Why only be angry at them?

segments.translation_text: Why were these non-virtues performed? Since all happiness and suffering depends on individuals’ good and bad karma, why should I be angry only at those who caused the harm? It is inappropriate to feel anger because:

segments.translation_html:
Seeing this, by all means,
I must create merit
That will develop in everyone
Thoughts of kindness for each other.

segments.translation_html:
For instance, when fire catches one house,
Run to the other house, where
It is right to take the straw
And other flammable things and throw them away.

segments.translation_html:
Likewise, when the mind becomes attached to anything,
The flames of hatred will arise.
From fear of burning merit.
It must be discarded immediately.

segments.translation_html:
Wouldn't it be better if one sentenced to decapitation Were freed with merely amputation? Wouldn't it be better if one in hell Were freed with merely human suffering?[p.214][[A Commentary on Shantideva's Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas]]
Gyaltsen, Lama Kalsang, and Ani Kunga Chodron, trans. ''A Commentary on Shantideva's Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas Written by Sazang Mati Panchen: Known as An Extremely Clear Illumination of the Meaning of the Text''. Walden, NY: Tsechen Kunchab Ling, 2019. First edition published by The Yeshe Dorje Foundation in 2006.

segments.wylie: dper na gsad par bya bar 'os pa'i mi zhig lag pa tsam bcad de btang nas gal te gsod pa las thar na cis ma legs te legs pa de bzhin du gal te mi yi sdug bsngal smod pa dang 'ching pa dang bsnun pa la sogs pa dang du blangs de bzod pa bsgoms pa nyid kyis ma 'ongs pa na dmyal pa myong bar 'gyur ba'i sdug bsngal chen po dang bral zhing zad par byas na cis ma legs te cis kyang legs pa nyid do/_/
segments.translation_text: If a person who had committed a crime punishable by execution were offered the chance to be freed with a lesser punishment such as the amputation of a hand, wouldn’t he consider himself fortunate? In the same way, by meditating patience, I can escape the great sufferings of hell by accepting the sufferings of the human realm, such as being criticized, bound, struck, etc. Isn’t it much better to choose meditation on patience? Thus I will be freed from great suffering and exhaust this current suffering.

segments.translation_html:
If I cannot tolerate
Even these present sufferings,
Why not restrain anger,
Which is the cause of the sufferings of hell?

segments.wylie: da lta mi'i lus thob pa'i dus su mi sdug pa dang phrad pa dang sdug pa dang bral ba la sogs pa'i sdug bsngal phra mo 'di tsam la'ang bdag gis bzod par mi nus par snang ba myong pas grub pa des na/_phyi ma la sems can dmyal ba'i sdug bsngal drag po myong bar 'gyur ba'i rgyu khro ba ci ste zlog mi byed de cis kyang bzlog par rigs so/_/
segments.translation_text: Now I have attained the opportunity of precious human birth. If I cannot tolerate the minor sufferings of encountering what I don’t want such as parting from loved ones, and coming across other things I do not want in this life, why not put a stop to this anger which is the cause of even more severe sufferings in the next life such as the severe sufferings of hell, etc.? Therefore, from every point of view, it is right to stop becoming angry.

segments.translation_html:
Although I have experienced the flames of hell
A thousand times for the purpose of desire.
Still, I have not accomplished either
My own or others' purpose.

segments.wylie: sngar 'dod yon la chags pa dang de dang 'gal ba las khros pa'i don du bsreg pa dang gcod pa dang 'bigs pa la sogs pa dmyal ba'i sdug bsngal lan stong phrag du ma myong bar gyur kyang bdag gis mthong ba dang ma mthong ba'i rang gi don dang ni phan pa dang bde ba'i mtshan nyid can gzhan gyi don yang ma byas pas ngal ba 'bras bu med par nges so/_/
segments.translation_text: As a result of being attached to desire objects and becoming angry when thwarted with respect to these, thousands of times I have experienced the suffering of being burned, slashed, pierced, and so forth in hell. All of this suffering produced no visible or invisible benefit or happiness for me or others. Certainly, it was fruitless hardship.

segments.translation_text: However, the hardship that arises from performing austerity for the purpose of achieving great enlightenment is not large, compared to the suffering of the hell realms. It has the great purpose of benefiting me and many other beings. On the basis of this suffering, the goal of Buddhahood will be accomplished, which will allow me to dispel the suffering of samsara for every sentient being. I should joyfully accept hardship for this purpose. Right patience toward such hardship is voluntarily performed only by Bodhisattvas.

segments.translation_text: If someone praises an enemy by describing his good qualities, the one who is described is happy, thinking that they have the good qualities described. If that is the case, O Mind, why don’t you feel the same happiness at hearing descriptions of the enemy’s good qualities? It is appropriate to feel joy, and it is inappropriate for the mind to burn with the fire of jealousy.

segments.translation_text: O Mind, the happiness that arises from feeling joy at other’s good qualities is the cause from which the result of happiness in the next life arises, and in this life, such joy is not contaminated by non-virtue. Such joy is a positive quality that is not prohibited and is permitted by the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. Therefore, it is right for Mahayana practitioners to feel joy at others’ good qualities without jealousy. It is also the best method of gathering beings into the path through gentle speech.

segments.translation_text: When someone praises another’s good qualities, the person who is praised feels happy. O Mind, under the influence of jealousy, if others’ happiness, which should be the cause of joy, makes you unhappy, you will not accomplish your own purpose. Such an attitude is like stopping the salary of servants who help you accomplish your own aims. Disregarding the very cause of your success will cause a decline in both the tangible result of success and happiness in this life, as well as the intangible result of happiness in the next life.

segments.wylie: ga' zhig gis rang gi yon tan brjod pa mthong ba'i tshe rjod pa po gzhan de la'ang bde ba 'dod par byed na thams cad du gzhan bde ba mi 'dod na 'gal zhing*/_yang 'ga' zhig gis gzhan gyi yon tan brjod pa mthong ba'i tshe phrag dog gi dbang gis rang la'ang bde ba mi 'dod cing yid mi bde bar byed na thams cad du rang nyid bde bar 'dod pa'ang 'gal bas/_'gal zhing mi rigs pa'i bsam pa de dag spangs te rang gzhan gnyi ga bde ba'i thabs la 'jug par rigs so/_/
segments.translation_text: When someone describes your good qualities, you agree with the delight of the describer, which contradicts your previous statement that you do not wish happiness for everyone. Again, when someone describes another person’s good qualities, due the power of jealousy, even one’s own happiness is not enjoyable, and the mind feels unpleasant. Doing so contradicts your wish for every aspect of happiness. Reflect on these inappropriate contradictions and abandon such thoughts in favor of rejoicing in happiness that comes to yourself and others.

segments.translation_html:
Enlightenment thought was generated
To wish happiness for all sentient beings, so
If sentient beings find their own happiness,
Why feel angry about it?

segments.wylie: sngar sems can thams cad la phan pa dang bde ba bsgrub par 'dod pas bsam pa byang chub kyi mchog tu ni sems bskyed pa blangs nas phyis sems can rnams kyis rang rang gis bde ba'i khyad par rnyed pa na/_des ko yid khyod ci ste khro bar byed de khro bar mi rigs pas dga' ba bskyed par bya'o/_/
segments.translation_text: Previously, when you made the excellent resolution of enlightenment thought, you wished to bring happiness and benefit to all sentient beings. Now when one of these beings is able to find a small portion of happiness on their own, why, O Mind, do you feel angry at them? Your anger and jealousy are unsuitable because instead you should feel happy and rejoice for them.

segments.wylie: sngar sems bskyed pa'i dus su 'dod pa dang gzugs dang gzugs med kyi 'jig rten gsum po ma lus pas mchod par 'os pa'i gnas su mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya bar sems can rnams thams cad la ni 'dod do zhes dam bcas nas/_da de lta bu lta zhog 'phral du gzhan la bsnyen bkur ngan ngon cung zad tsam byed pa mthong nas ci'i phyir de la mi bzod par gdung zhing khro bar byed de khro bar mi rigs so/_/
segments.translation_text: Previously, at the time of taking the vow, I made the great aspiration that every sentient being would achieve perfect enlightenment, and be venerated by every being in the three realms (the desire, form, and formless realms) without exception. Having made such a commitment, why am I impatient and angry at seeing the minor success of material gain or temporary ordinary veneration, needless to say the ultimate result of perfect enlightenment? This is inappropriate.

segments.translation_text: If you are displeased when a being receives temporary veneration for a minor purpose, this seriously contradicts your aspiration that they attain perfect enlightenment. How could a person who is jealous and angry at others’ success and material gain possibly have generated excellent enlightenment thought? Such an attitude demonstrates that it does not exist. Therefore, having made the commitment of enlightenment thought, discard thoughts of jealousy.

segments.translation_text: Why discard the merit arising from previous giving, the faith arising from pure conduct, and the good quality of wishing others’ benefit and happiness due to jealousy? It is wrong to discard them. If by all means one desires material gain, then the cause of exalted material gain is the root of virtue. Tell me why you are not angry at jealousy which does not cherish the root of your virtue. It is not right to feel angry toward others.
segments.source_html: སྔོན་གྱི་སྦྱིན་པ་ལས་བྱུང་བའི་བསོད་ནམས་དང་ནི་སྤྱོད་པ་རྣམ་དག་ལས་བྱུང་བའི་དད་པ༵་དང་གཞན་ལ་ཕན་བདེ་འདོད་པའི་རང་གི་ཡོན་ཏན་རྣམས་ཕྲག་དོག་གི་སྒོ་ནས་ཅིའི་ཕྱིར་འདོ༵ར་ཏེ་འདོར་བར་མི་རིགས་ཤིང༌། ཅི་ནས་རྙེད་པ་ཐོབ་པར་འདོད་ན་རྙེད་པ་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ་ཐོབ་པར་འགྱུར་བའི་རྒྱུ་དགེ་བའི་རྩ་བ་དེ་དག་མི་འཛིན་པ༵འི་ཕྲག་དོག་ཅན་རང་ཉིད་ལ་རྒྱུ་མཚན་གང་གིས་ཁྲོ་བར་མི་བྱེད་པ་སྨྲོ༵ས་ཏེ་ཁྲོ་བར་བྱའི་གཞན་ལ་ནི་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །[p.-199][[རབ་གསལ་སྣང་བ་]]

segments.translation_text: Why do you not only lack regret at previous sins such as taking what was not given, which is the cause of being unable to obtain material, but still wish to compete with others who are accumulating great merit which is the cause of successful material gain? It is unsuitable to compete. If competition is desired, exert yourself in accumulating a heap of merit, which is the cause.

segments.translation_text: O Mind, if your wish that the enemy will suffer is accomplished, why feel joy in it? There is no reason to feel joy. You may think, l‘My wish is fulfilled, so I am satisfied,” but there is nothing worse than this evil thought, as it will cause falling into lower rebirth.

segments.translation_text: As fishermen catch fish by catching their throats with a sharp hook and dragging them, so have the fishermen that are the defilements caught me on the sharp hook of evil karma. Its unbearable hook will drag me into hell where for a long time I will experience the terrible sufferings of being boiled in the cauldrons of hell, or dragged about on the molten ground by the messengers of the lord of death.

segments.translation_text: Some may think, "I should feel angry toward those who interfere with my praise and renown.” This is also inappropriate. Wishing for others’ praise through description of my good qualities, and veneration through proclaiming my fame will not attain any of these five goals: neither increased merit for the next life, nor lengthening of this life, nor increase in strength and robustness, nor good physical health, nor even temporary physical comfort.

segments.translation_text: In case one knows of these five goals and wishes to obtain them for their own purpose, what is the use of praise and renown? These are not the method of accomplishing any of them. However, if one thinks, "Praise and fame will bring temporary mental happiness, and I want to get that,” then one would also engage in other causes of temporary mental happiness such as gambling, wrong livelihood, prostitution, drinking alcohol, etc. All of these are unsuitable.

segments.translation_html:
For the purpose of fame,
One spends wealth and may even be killed.
What use are those words?
After death, who will enjoy them?

segments.translation_text: Some deluded ones who lack good qualities, desiring to become renowned, give away their valuables, like elephants, as if they were pieces of straw. Desiring to become renowned as brave, they even dare to enter the battlefield where they may be killed. What use are pleasant words of fame? They are of no benefit whatsoever because after death, fame will not bring comfort or happiness to either body or mind.

segments.translation_text: To the extent that the person who praises me feels happy, I might think that I feel happy because their happiness has been transferred to me. But this is not true. segments.translation_text: One may think that happiness is felt due to rejoicing in the happiness of the person who praises me, but if that were the case, why wouldn’t one feel the same joy at the happiness of all sentient beings? Why feel uncomfortable and jealous when someone experiences the happiness of praising an enemy’s good qualities? It is not right to feel uncomfortable in this way.

segments.translation_text: Words of praise have no mental consciousness. Furthermore, the happiness in others’ minds cannot be transferred to oneself. Feeling joy and pleasure when praised, respected, and flattered by others causes the defilement of attachment to arise. Analyzed carefully, these words are of no benefit. They are like the sand castles that children build and become attached to. They have no meaning or essence.

If one wishes to gain merit, then exert oneself in the practice of patience.

segments.translation_html: Generally, no phenomena appear in the absence of their prior causes, and they do appear when preceded by those causes. Thus it is ascertained that prior phenomena are the cause of accomplishing the next. If that is the case, how could a cause be considered a hindrance to its result? This is illogical.

segments.translation_text: Especially, patience cannot be accomplished in the absence of causers of harm. That patience exists because of those causers of harm. So, those causers of harm are ascertained to be the direct causers of the accomplishment of patience. Therefore, how could they be said to interfere with the development of patience? It is inappropriate to regard them as negative; they should be regarded as favorable conditions.

segments.translation_text: Having accomplished great merit by successfully developing patience as the antidote to anger using this enemy as the object, first and foremost, dedicate the merit to that enemy. This is because the causer of harm is the cause of accomplishing patience, which is the ultimate austerity. segments.translation_text: Then one may think, "The holy Dharma does not have the intention to harm, but enemies have harmful thoughts toward me, so it is not suitable to venerate them.” However, if all enemies had no thoughts of harm, and like an excellent physician always brought only happiness, benefit, and favorable conditions, how could the meditation of patience be accomplished, as there would be no harm that is the cause of patience?

segments.translation_text: Since patience cannot be accomplished based on those who exert only benefit, and patience arises based on those who cause harm and have hateful minds, therefore, enemies themselves are the direct cause of accomplishing patience, which is the most exalted among noble austerities. Although they do not have the intention to assist by being the cause of patience, still they are as suitable to venerate as the holy Dharma, because they are the cause of accomplishing virtue.

As both Victors and sentient beings
Are equal in causing a Buddha’s accomplishment,
Since Buddhas are respected,
Why not sentient beings in the same manner?

segments.translation_text: One may wonder, "How could sentient beings, who are full of defilements, be equal to the Buddha, who is perfectly enlightened?” This case does not measure the quality of their motivation; it measures them as equal in that they are causes of accomplishing great enlightenment, which is the result. From that aspect, sentient beings possess a good quality equal to that of the Buddha, so they are explained as fields that are equal in accomplishing the harvest of virtue.

segments.translation_html:
Venerating those who possess enlightenment thought Is the greatness of sentient beings. The merit of devotion to the Buddhas Is the greatness of the Buddhas.[p.227][[A Commentary on Shantideva's Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas]]
Gyaltsen, Lama Kalsang, and Ani Kunga Chodron, trans. ''A Commentary on Shantideva's Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas Written by Sazang Mati Panchen: Known as An Extremely Clear Illumination of the Meaning of the Text''. Walden, NY: Tsechen Kunchab Ling, 2019. First edition published by The Yeshe Dorje Foundation in 2006.

segments.translation_text: Thus the greatness of sentient beings is the merit that can be attained by benefiting and serving them with a mind of loving kindness. The greatness of the fully enlightened Bhagwan Buddhas is the merit that can be attained from venerating them and making offerings to them with a mind of faith.

Needless to say it is suitable to venerate them with ordinary offerings.

segments.translation_text: Another reason to please sentient beings is that Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, who perform inconceivable benefit for oneself and all sentient beings, are the exalted spiritual friends of limitless sentient beings, without deceit or cunning. For those who wish to repay their kindness, there is no method other than pleasing sentient beings. By what other means can the Buddhas be repaid? There is none, and so therefore I must please sentient beings. The holy ones have given their bodies, limbs, and even heads as gifts solely for the happiness and benefit of sentient beings, and performed such great austerities that they even dared to enter Avici hell to benefit others.

segments.translation_html: Another reason to please sentient beings is that Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, who perform inconceivable benefit for oneself and all sentient beings, are the exalted spiritual friends of limitless sentient beings, without deceit or cunning. For those who wish to repay their kindness, there is no method other than pleasing sentient beings. By what other means can the Buddhas be repaid? There is none, and so therefore I must please sentient beings. The holy ones have given their bodies, limbs, and even heads as gifts solely for the happiness and benefit of sentient beings, and performed such great austerities that they even dared to enter Avici hell to benefit others.

segments.translation_text: If the Buddhas and their Noble Sons, who are the lords of me and all sentient beings, perform only the benefit of others, disregarding hardship even to their own holy bodies, why should I not respect these beings? Should one such as me, who am deluded about the nature of reality and dominated by ignorance, feel conceited toward them? I must not, and I must respectfully serve them as a servant, following the Buddha’s advice.

segments.translation_html:
Making them happy causes all Buddhas pleasure.
Harming displeases them.
Therefore, by pleasing them, all Buddhas are pleased.
By harming them, all Buddhas are harmed.

segments.translation_text: The Lords of Sages are pleased at seeing that sentient beings, who are like their only children, are happy. The Lords of Sages are displeased at seeing that sentient beings are unhappy due to harm. Therefore, benefiting sentient beings and making them happy is the best method of pleasing all the Buddhas. If one causes suffering by harming those sentient beings, it also harms the Lords of Sages.

segments.translation_text: Previously, under the influence of ignorance, I harmed countless beings through my body, voice, and mind. This was a great sin and has displeased the greatly compassionate Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. From this time onward, in the presence of the great Protectors, I confess each of these sins individually with a feeling of regret. I resolve to refrain in the future. I request the Lord of Sages and his Noble Sons to forgive all of those things that have caused them displeasure and contradicted their holy intent.

segments.translation_html:
In order to act to please the Tathagatas,
From now on. I shall be a well-tamed servant of the world.
Even if many beings kick my head or step on me, I will not retaliate.
May the Protector of the World be pleased.

segments.wylie: da ni de bzhin gshegs pa sras dang bcas pa rnams bzhed pa bzhin bsgrubs pas mnyes par bgyi ba'i slad du dus deng nas nges par bzung ste lus ngag yid gsum gyi 'jig rten gsum po mtha' dag gi bran dang 'dra ba nyid du mchi bar bgyi'o/_/des na 'gro ba mang po'i rdog pas bdag gi spyi bor rdung zhing 'tshog gam 'gums shing gsod par bgyid kyang lan mi bsdo bar gus pas dang du blang bar bgyi yis 'jig rten gsum gyi mgon po thugs rje chen po dang ldan pa rnams thugs dgyes par mdzod cig ces pa'o/_/
segments.translation_text: From now onward, I will practice according to the teachings of the Tathagatas and their Noble Sons. In order to please them, from now onward, I will truly act as the servant of all sentient beings in the three worlds through my body, voice, and mind. Doing so, I will not retaliate against other sentient beings, no matter how many types of harm they cause me, whether kicking my head. striking me, or even taking my life, I will voluntarily accept them as objects of respect. Thus may I please the Protectors of the Three Worlds, the possessors of great compassion.

segments.translation_text: The suchness of the fully enlightened Buddha, the embodiment of great compassion toward all sentient beings without exception, is known as the self that has been purified of self. The Buddha’s suchness is the same as the suchness of all sentient beings. There is no doubt or question of this whatsoever. Therefore, as it is said, "Sentient beings are the Buddha.”

segments.translation_text: Pleasing sentient beings, as extensively explained above through logic, is the method of pleasing the Tathagatas and is also an offering of practice according to their advice. Benefiting sentient beings is the direct cause of perfectly accomplishing the accumulation of merit for one’s own purpose. Through pleasing other beings, it is possible to bring them into the right path; therefore this is an excellent method of dispelling all types of suffering of worldly beings. For these reasons, I must always strive to perform actions that please sentient beings.

therefore this is an excellent method of dispelling all types of suffering of worldly beings. For these reasons, I must always strive to perform actions that please sentient beings.

segments.translation_text: As a metaphor, a cruel and harsh king must be pleased by various methods by ordinary subjects. In the same way, sentient beings that have various wishes must be pleased by various methods. The reason is that even if a king is displeased and angered, all that he can do is to harm body and wealth in this life, whereas, displeasing sentient beings brings the suffering of hell in the next life. Could a king cause such destruction? He could not.

segments.translation_html:
While in samsara, patience brings a handsome body,
Lack of illness, fame,
Long life, and the attainment of
The great happiness of a universal emperor.

segments.wylie: sangs rgyas ma thob kyi bar du 'khor bar gnas pa'i tshe yang bzod pa bsgoms par gyur bas gzugs mdzes shing blta na sdug pa yid du 'ong ba dang yan lag dang nying lag dang dbang po thams cad tshang ba la sogs pa dang*/_nad sna tshogs kyis yongs su gdung ba med pa dang*/_grags pa'am dga' ba rgya chen po 'phel ba dang*/_tshe shin tu yun ring por bde bar 'tsho ba dang rin po che sna bdun dang*/_nye bar rin po che sna bdun la sogs pa'i 'byor ba dang bka' 'bangs su gtogs pa rnams dge ba bcu la 'god nus pa'i 'khor los sgyur ba'i rgyal srid kyi bde ba rgyas pa phun sum tshogs pa thob cing*/_sngar bshad pa ltar mthar thug byang chub chen po thob pa la sogs pa'o/_/
segments.translation_text: By practicing patience until Buddhahood is attained, even while remaining in samsara, one will have a beautiful and enticingly attractive physical form. In every rebirth, one will be born with perfect sense organs, limbs well formed, free of disease, with increasing happiness and renown, live a long healthy life, and acquire wealth, such as the seven precious jewels and seven semi-precious jewels. One’s relatives and associates will be able to be brought into the path of ten virtues, and the success, happiness, and possessions of a universal emperor will flourish. As explained earlier, the ultimate benefit is becoming able to achieve great enlightenment.
